reason: The cited evidence supports that TRIP and nano-twinning enhance strength-ductility-toughness combinations in CrCoNi-based HEAs (E1, E3, E8) and that small-scale HEAs can have high Young's modulus (E7), but no evidence is provided for the core premise that a dual-phase (bcc+hcp) nano-lamellar microstructure can be achieved or that it yields the claimed simultaneous property improvements; several citations are irrelevant to the hypothesis (E2, E4, E5, E6).
premises: Dual-phase (bcc+hcp) nano-lamellar microstructures can be induced in HEAs by tailored thermo-mechanical processing and compositional control.
Such nano-lamellar architectures promote strain partitioning and activate TRIP and nano-twinning mechanisms.
Activation of TRIP and nano-twinning enhances work hardening, delays crack propagation, and improves load distribution.
This microstructural design simultaneously boosts strength, ductility, Young's modulus, and fracture resistance.
The predicted improvements are measurable (e.g., 10-20% yield strength increase, 15-30% ductility increase) over single-phase HEAs or stainless steels.
